active_validators.definition: Number of validators currently in the active set of the network's consensus layer.
active_validators.avalanche: platform.getCurrentValidators result length (Primary Network; the returned 'weight' already includes delegated stake — delegatorWeight is a subset, never added on top).
active_validators.polygon_pos: Heimdall v2 /stake/validators-set validator count (CometBFT active set).
active_validators.limits: Counts validator records, not independent organizations. One entity may run several validators; one validator may be operated by a third party (e.g. exchange staking products).

top10_share.definition: Sum of the 10 largest stake weights divided by total active weight.
top10_share.polygon_pos_unit: Heimdall voting power (= staked POL / 10^15, verified against staking-api totals)
top10_share.limits: Weight share ≠ organization share. Same caveat as active_validators.

max_share.definition: Largest single validator's share of total active weight.

nakamoto_concentration.definition: Minimum number of the largest validators whose combined weight reaches a threshold of total weight. Reported at 33% and 50%.
nakamoto_concentration.formula: min n such that sum(sort_desc(weight)[0:n]) / sum(weight) >= threshold
nakamoto_concentration.what_it_shows: How few validators dominate the stake-weight distribution.
nakamoto_concentration.what_it_does_not_show: It is NOT an attack-cost estimate and NOT a universal attack threshold. Different consensus models convert weight control into concrete capabilities differently.
nakamoto_concentration.polygon_pos_reading: Heimdall runs CometBFT: >1/3 of voting power can halt checkpoint/milestone finality; >2/3 can finalize arbitrary conflicting state at the consensus layer. Bor block production is a separate control (see block_producers).
nakamoto_concentration.avalanche_reading: Snowman-family consensus is probabilistic/metastable with stake-sampled leaders; published analysis bounds safety probabilistically (Snow whitepaper). 33%/50% figures are labeled concentration statistics only.

block_producers.definition: Validators that actually produce execution-layer blocks in the current window.
block_producers.polygon_pos: Heimdall 'veBlop': validator votes (stake-weighted positional tally) elect a candidate pool (limit 4 since the SetProducerDowntime hardfork); each Bor span (6400 blocks) freezes exactly ONE producer, rotating round-robin over the pool. Observed producers are read from /bor/spans/{id} — never hardcoded. If the vote map is empty the heimdalld client falls back to a compiled-in list (currently '91,92,93,94').
block_producers.avalanche: Different consensus model: no fixed producer set. C-Chain/P-Chain blocks are proposed by stake-sampled leaders (Snowman++ proposer-VM); every validator can propose in proportion to its weight. Not directly comparable to Bor spans.
block_producers.limits: A Bor producer orders/censors transactions within its span (~3.6 h); it cannot alone finalize history (Heimdall checkpoints/milestones need 2/3+ voting power), change protocol rules, or move user funds. The span producer set is per-span, not a permanent list of the only validators that can ever produce blocks.

protocol_upgrade_control.definition: Who can change consensus rules / contract logic, through which mechanism.
protocol_upgrade_control.polygon_pos: Three layers: (1) L1 contracts (StakeManager/RootChain) are UpgradableProxies whose owner is a TimelockController; the timelock's PROPOSER+EXECUTOR is a Gnosis Safe with threshold 5-of-9, and getMinDelay() was 0 s on 2026-11-12 — 5 of 9 signers can upgrade staking/checkpoint contract logic with no waiting period. StakingInfo/StateSender/SlashManager are directly owned by the same Safe. (2) Heimdall module params require the x/gov authority (validator-weighted voting). (3) heimdalld hardfork heights are compiled into client binaries and activate when validators adopt the release.
protocol_upgrade_control.avalanche: No on-chain admin key for Primary Network consensus rules. Named upgrades (Apricot..Helicon) activate at timestamps compiled into avalanchego; validators must adopt new client software. Control concentrates in client development and release coordination (Ava Labs) plus validator adoption — not in a multisig. 'No multisig' does not mean 'no centralization risk'.
protocol_upgrade_control.limits: Contract upgrade authority is not a key over user wallets, and multisig membership counts are addresses, not verified real-world identities. Software-upgrade influence is social/technical, not an on-chain threshold.

entity_concentration.definition: Concentration after mapping validators to operating entities.
entity_concentration.reason: No authoritative validator→entity registry exists for either network. Operator-declared names (Polygon staking API) are display-only and cannot be used to merge validators (names can be duplicated, renamed, or false). Address or name similarity is not evidence of common control. If a reliable mapping is ever published, this metric can be added.

data_quality.update_cadence: Every 6 hours via GitHub Actions (scheduled runs are best-effort; GitHub does not guarantee exact timing).
data_quality.failure_policy: A failed collection never overwrites the last valid snapshot. The page shows the age of the data and any collection errors.
data_quality.anomaly_policy: Validator count or total weight moving >50% between snapshots is flagged as a suspected data anomaly: recorded in history but not promoted to the official latest stats.
data_quality.reproducibility: Every snapshot stores the sorted weight vector it was computed from, the chain heights, and the endpoint list, so all shares and concentration counts can be recomputed independently.
